title: Level 3 Geography — Natural Processes and Landscapes 2025
subject: geography

questions.text:
Name a New Zealand geographic environment to use to answer both parts of the question.

Use the space provided to draw an annotated map(s) and/or diagram(s) of your environment to explain how interacting natural processes have shaped ONE natural feature.
questions.expectedAnswer: Draw annotated map/diagram of a named NZ environment explaining how interacting natural processes shape one natural feature.
questions.markingGuide: Not Achieved (N1-N2): Relevant natural feature identified with limited evidence. Does not adequately analyse processes. Achievement (A3-A4): Includes some supporting case study evidence with some detail. Partially analyses the operation and interaction of processes to shape natural features. Merit (M5-M6): Includes detailed supporting evidence. Analyses in detail the operation and interaction of processes to shape natural features of a NZ geographic environment. Excellence (E7-E8): Insightful analysis with comprehensive, integrated supporting case study evidence, drawing conclusions about how processes shape the feature.

questions.text:
Analyse how interacting natural processes operate in your environment to shape a second, different, natural feature from that identified in part (a).

Your response to part (b) should include:
- the name of your second natural feature — this must be different from the feature in part (a)
- how natural processes operate and interact to create and shape this second natural feature
- integrated comprehensive supporting case study evidence.
questions.expectedAnswer: Analyses how interacting natural processes shape a second, different natural feature in the same NZ environment.
questions.markingGuide: Not Achieved (N1-N2): Describes natural processes and environment but provides little or no evidence. Achievement (A3-A4): Includes some supporting case study evidence with some detail. Partially analyses the operation and interaction of processes. Merit (M5-M6): Analyses in detail the operation and interaction of processes with detailed supporting case study evidence. Excellence (E7-E8): Analyses with insight the operation and interaction of processes within a named NZ environment, drawing conclusions about natural features. Integrates comprehensive evidence throughout.
